sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The institutionalization of e-governance has been heralded as a democratizing panacea capable of eradicating bureaucratic inertia, minimizing administrative corruption, and streamlining public service delivery. By digitizing citizen-state interfaces, modern governments can bypass predatory intermediaries, ensuring that welfare disbursements, identity verifications, and regulatory approvals reach intended beneficiaries directly. However, this hyper-digital pivot exposes a deep systemic fault line: the digital divide, where marginalized populations lacking internet connectivity and digital literacy are effectively disenfranchised from state mechanisms. When essential civic resources become exclusively accessible through digital portals, the state inadvertently transforms technological privilege into a prerequisite for basic citizenship rights. Furthermore, centralized data architectural frameworks used for e-governance create massive surveillance apparatuses that significantly blur the boundaries between public welfare and invasive state monitoring. The true metric of successful e-governance is therefore not the sophistication of its algorithms or portals, but its structural inclusivity and its commitment to safeguarding civil liberties against digital overreach.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The relentless march of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) into professional domains has triggered a paradigm shift in global labor dynamics, moving far beyond the automation of routine manual tasks. Historically, technological disruptions primarily displaced blue-collar labor; however, contemporary cognitive computing aggressively targets the white-collar vanguard, executing sophisticated data synthesis, legal document drafting, and algorithmic financial analysis with disconcerting efficacy. While techno-optimists champion this transition as a liberation of human intellect—arguing that AI will subsume mundane analytical friction and elevate workers to higher-tier strategic roles—the velocity of this displacement threatens to outpace systemic re-skilling frameworks. This temporal mismatch risks exacerbating socioeconomic bifurcation, creating a precarious class of highly educated yet functionally obsolete professionals. Furthermore, the corporate imperative to optimize profit margins via algorithmic labor introduces a profound ethical vacuum regarding worker agency and institutional accountability. The ultimate challenge lies not in halting algorithmic integration, but in architecting proactive social safety nets and dynamic educational curricula that treat human capital not as a static resource, but as an adaptable partner to cognitive machines.

questions.q: The phrase “democratizing panacea” shows that e-governance is initially seen as
opts: a system that will increase corruption
a cure-all for bureaucratic delays and poor service delivery
a tool only for tech-savvy groups
a corporate takeover of state assets
questions.why: A panacea is a remedy for everything. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Complete digitisation of public services risks
opts: disenfranchising people who lack digital access and literacy
ending the state's ability to monitor approvals
questions.why: Third sentence: the digital divide. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: When access to state services becomes exclusively digital, the author warns that
opts: technological privilege becomes a prerequisite for basic citizenship rights
the state loses its data authority
questions.why: Fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: What dual nature of e-governance is highlighted?
opts: It cuts trade barriers but raises inflation
It streamlines welfare delivery but also enables invasive surveillance
It removes corruption but empowers intermediaries
It raises farm output but ignores cities
questions.why: Second and fifth sentences. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the final sentence, good e-governance is measured by its
opts: inclusiveness and protection against digital overreach
questions.why: Last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's main concern about the “velocity of this displacement” is that
opts: it will end human strategic decision-making
workers will refuse to learn AI tools
re-skilling programmes cannot keep pace with AI adoption
blue-collar workers will be pushed into white-collar roles
questions.why: Displacement “threatens to outpace systemic re-skilling frameworks”. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: “Socioeconomic bifurcation” implies that AI could
opts: split society into two unequal economic segments
questions.why: Bifurcation means splitting in two. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Techno-optimists see AI as a way to
opts: relieve workers of routine cognitive tasks so they can focus on strategy
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which statement is TRUE according to the passage?
opts: Past disruptions hit white-collar workers more
The corporate drive for algorithmic labour raises ethical concerns about worker agency and accountability
The author wants AI integration stopped
Generative AI cannot draft legal documents
questions.why: Fifth sentence; the others contradict the text. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's tone toward the future of human labour is best described as
opts: cautionary yet focused on structural adaptation
questions.why: It warns of risks and proposes safety nets and new curricula. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Identify the incorrect sentence:
opts: Ten kilometers is a long distance.
The committee has reached a decision.
The police is investigating the case.
questions.why: 'Police' is always plural: 'The police are'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “She ____ have informed us earlier; the delay caused confusion.”
questions.why: A past duty not done: 'should have'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the idiom that best replaces the underlined idea: “The project failed due to poor planning.”
questions.why: 'Fell flat' means failed completely. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “People believe him to be dishonest.”
opts: He is believed to be dishonest.
questions.why: Present 'believe' becomes 'is believed', infinitive kept. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “candid”:
questions.why: Candid means open and honest. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The Poonamallee–Vadapalani stretch inaugurated by the PM on 11 October 2026 is part of which metro network?
questions.why: It includes a 3.7-km double-decker structure. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The 'JOSH' (Joint Squad for Health) teams launched in October 2026 are part of:
opts: Pradhan Mantri TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan

questions.q: At which position did India finish on the medal table of the 2026 Asian Games?
questions.why: 21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze: 85 medals. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The International Day of the Girl Child is observed on:
questions.why: National Girl Child Day in India is 24 January.

questions.q: Who presented the President's Colour to Goa Police in 2026?
questions.why: The President's Colour is the highest honour for a police force.

questions.q: Exercise Udara Shakti 2026 was an air exercise between India and:
questions.why: Held at Subang Air Base, 10–14 August 2026.

questions.q: The outlay of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) was raised in 2026 to about:
The Living Planet Report 2026 is released by:
India's BRICS chairship in 2026 was its:
questions.why: The 18th summit was held in New Delhi.

questions.q: In computing, 'HTTP' stands for:
questions.why: Static computers.

questions.q: A price rises 25%, then falls 20%, then rises 10%. What is the overall increase?
Karan beats Arjun by 10 m in a 100 m race. In a second race Karan starts 10 m behind the line. What happens?
questions.why: Speeds 100 : 90. While Karan runs 110 m, Arjun runs 99 m. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2024.

questions.q: Item A costs ₹3.20 in 2008 and rises 50 paise a year; item B costs ₹5.30 and rises 25 paise a year. In which year will A cost 40 paise more than B?
questions.why: The gap closes 25 paise a year from −₹2.10 to +₹0.40: 2.50 ÷ 0.25 = 10 years → 2018. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2023.

questions.q: Rice at ₹15/kg and ₹20/kg is mixed in the ratio 2 : 3. What is the price per kg of the mixture?
The present worth of a sum is ₹576 and the banker's gain is ₹16. What is the true discount?
questions.why: TD² = PW × BG = 576 × 16 = 9216, so TD = 96. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2023.

questions.q: 4 men and 6 women finish a work in 8 days; 3 men and 7 women in 10 days. In how many days will 10 women finish it?
questions.why: 8(4m + 6w) = 10(3m + 7w), so m = 11w. Work = 400 woman-days; 10 women take 40 days. GPSC CBRT, Dec 2023.

questions.q: If CAT is written DBU, how is DOG written?
questions.why: Each letter +1. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which completes the series? 4, 13, 40, 121, 364, ___
godabim = kidney stones; romzbim = kidney beans; romzbako = wax beans. Which word could mean 'wax statue'?
questions.why: bim = kidney, romz = beans, bako = wax; the noun comes first, so 'statue' + bako. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: According to §150, a patient complaining of one or a few trivial symptoms of recent origin, removable by a change of diet or regimen, has:
opts: an indisposition, not a real disease needing medicine
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §150: indispositions need only removal of the exciting cause.

questions.q: Hahnemann's 'Lesser Writings' were collected and translated into English by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Dudgeon also translated the Organon (fifth edition).

questions.q: 'The Science of Therapeutics according to the Principles of Homoeopathy' was written by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Carroll Dunham's philosophical lectures.

questions.q: Thirst for large quantities of cold water at long intervals, stitching pains worse from the slightest motion, and irritability with a wish to be left alone suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Bryonia: large drinks at long intervals.

questions.q: Sudden, sharp cutting neuralgic pains around the eye, worse from touch and motion, with palpitation, call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Spigelia: left-sided neuralgia, heart and eye.

questions.q: Sticky, stringy, tough mucus that can be drawn into long threads, as in sinusitis or bronchitis, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Kali bich: ropy discharges, pains in small spots.

questions.q: Coldness, emaciation and night sweats in a timid, yielding patient who lacks grit and has slow-healing wounds call for:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Silicea: lack of grit, suppuration.

questions.q: Homoeopathic medicines should be stored:
opts: away from sunlight and strong-smelling substances such as camphor and perfumes
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Light, heat and strong odours can spoil potencies.

questions.q: Medicated globules are prepared by:
opts: pouring the liquid potency on unmedicated globules so they are evenly moistened
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. The vehicle is then dried.

questions.q: In repertorisation, the 'totality of symptoms' is best understood as:
opts: the characteristic symptoms forming a complete picture of the patient
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Weighted characteristic symptoms, not a mere count.

questions.q: A card repertory (such as Boger's or Kishore's) works by:
opts: listing remedies under disease names only
lining up punched cards, one per symptom, so that remedies common to all show through
printing all rubrics in one volume
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Card repertories use the elimination of remedies by punched cards.

questions.q: The glomerular filtration rate is measured most accurately by the clearance of:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Inulin is filtered but neither reabsorbed nor secreted; PAH measures renal plasma flow.

questions.q: The hormone that raises blood sugar during fasting and is secreted by the alpha cells of the pancreas is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It promotes glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis.

questions.q: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) is typically very high in:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. ESR rises with raised globulins and fibrinogen; it falls in polycythaemia and sickle cell disease.

questions.q: The organism causing leptospirosis is transmitted mainly through:
opts: contact with water or soil contaminated by rat urine
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Common after floods in Goa and other monsoon states.

questions.q: Episodic throbbing one-sided headache with nausea and sensitivity to light suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. May be preceded by an aura.

questions.q: Hypertension with a full, bounding pulse, flushed face and throbbing headache, worse from heat, may suggest homoeopathically:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Glonoine: congestion, pulsation.

questions.q: Asthma attacks from 1 to 3 a.m. with anxiety and restlessness, relieved by sitting up and warm drinks, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Arsenicum: after-midnight aggravation, anxiety.

questions.q: Postpartum haemorrhage is defined as blood loss after vaginal delivery of more than:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. More than 1000 mL after caesarean section.

questions.q: Physiological jaundice in a term newborn usually disappears by:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Prolonged jaundice needs evaluation.

questions.q: Fracture of the neck of the femur is most common in:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. From minor falls.

questions.q: The commonest cause of hearing loss in children is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. 'Glue ear'.

questions.q: Herd immunity refers to:
opts: protection of a population when a high proportion is immune, which reduces spread
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Indirect protection of the unimmunised.

questions.q: Under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, the National Register of homoeopathic practitioners is maintained by the:
opts: Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy
Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. The NCH Act 2020 replaced the HCC Act 1973 and set up three autonomous boards.

questions.q: Under the homoeopathy practitioners' code of ethics, a registered practitioner is expected to:
opts: display registration details and practise only in his or her own system
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Practitioners must not cross over into other systems except as allowed by law.
